title: Starfall, a browser game built from scratch
brief: Build a small browser game from scratch, in the folder ~/Projects/starfall. The game: you steer a little ship along the bottom of the screen, dodge falling stars and catch energy orbs; the stars fall faster as the score climbs. Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript only, in that one folder: no libraries and no internet. Run every command in your own terminal with the shell's agent_run action, never the Terminal app's run action. It is called like this: os_act {"app": "shell", "action": "agent_run", "args": {"command": "mkdir -p ~/Projects/starfall"}}. Use it for every file and every command: first `mkdir -p ~/Projects/starfall`, then write a short plan to ~/Projects/starfall/PLAN.md as a checklist of about eight steps (lines starting with '- [ ] '), from an empty page to a finished game with a start screen, score, levels, keyboard and touch controls, and sound that is off until the player turns it on. Then work through the plan one step at a time: write or change the files with agent_run, open ~/Projects/starfall/index.html in the browser to check what you made, fix what you see, and tick the step off in PLAN.md by changing its '- [ ] ' to '- [x] '. People are watching the screen, so keep each step small and visible. When every step is ticked and the game plays well, say FINISHED on its own line.
keep_going: Keep going on Starfall. Read ~/Projects/starfall/PLAN.md with the shell's agent_run action, for example os_act {"app": "shell", "action": "agent_run", "args": {"command": "cat ~/Projects/starfall/PLAN.md"}}. If it does not exist yet, create the folder and the plan first, as the brief said. Otherwise take the first step that is not ticked, do it with agent_run, check it in the browser, then tick it off in PLAN.md. If every step is ticked and the game plays well from the start screen to game over, say FINISHED on its own line.
